name: Paniya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Somasekharan Nair, P. Paniya Bhasha (descriptive study of Paniya incl. phonology; Glottolog cites Nair 1985); print-only, Shodhganga unreachable (ECONNREFUSED)

sources.citation: Sen, Aparajita. 2023. Paniya. In Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India (ed.), Linguistic Survey of India – Tamil Nadu, pp. 506-584. New Delhi: ORGI. (survey Dec 2021-Jan 2022; based on the LSI/MTSI report consolidated by S. Kunjamma, Univ. of Kerala)
sources.note: Section 2 Phonology (pp. 511-530) covers phoneme inventory, contrasts, 2.8 Suprasegmental Features (p. 528) and 2.9 Syllable structure. 2.8 says only 'In Paniya language suprasegmentals are represented in length' and then lists long vowels by position; the words stress/accent/tone/intonation do not occur anywhere in the chapter.
sources.venue: Linguistic Survey of India – Tamil Nadu

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Paniya language' (wikitext via API, 2026-09-17) and Glottolog 5.3 languoid page pani1256
sources.note: No phonology. Used only for bibliography: it lists Vijay Arul 2019 (Shodhganga) and Kapp 2020 (Harrassowitz), which led to the two opened/identified descriptions above; Glottolog lists only Lawrence 1979, Nair 1977, Nair 1985, Ethnologue.

sources.citation: Vijay Arul, M. 2019. The Endangered Tribal Language Paniya – An Ethnolinguistic Study. PhD thesis, CAS in Linguistics, Annamalai University (supervisor P. Vijaya). Shodhganga hdl 10603/283045.
sources.note: Ch. IV 'Linguistic Profile of Paniya Language' (pp. 53-116): 'Paniya language has 31 phonemes, of which 29 are segmental phonemes and 2 are supra-segmental phonemes' (p. 53); 4.1.2 (p. 55): 'The supra-segmental phonemes of Paniya are of two types, viz. juncture and length.' Syllable section 4.3 (pp. 65-68) gives templates only. No mention of stress or accent in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent full chapter text). Data from Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu) Paniya.

sources.citation: Syam S.K., Arun Kumar K.P. et al. (KIRTADS, Kozhikode). 2018/2021. Paniya Language Primer Parts II-III (Anganvadi, Standard I, Standard II handbooks). Malayalam-Paniya bilingual primers.
sources.note: School primers in Malayalam script; no phonological description, nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent Malayalam and English stress terms negative).

sources.citation: Mohanlal, Sam. 2001. Mother tongue education and psycho-societal involvement in tribal communities: a case study of Paniya tribe. Language in India 1(3).
sources.note: Education/sociolinguistics; no phonology, 'stress' occurs only in the psychological sense.

sources.note: The source named by an earlier compilation and Glottolog's grammar sketch; a Malayalam-language descriptive study of the Wayanad (Kerala) variety, which neither opened source covers; may contain a note on ഊന്നൽ/സ്വരാഘാതം (stress).

sources.citation: Kapp, Dieter B. 2020. Paṇiya: Grammatik, Textproben und Wörterbuch. Beiträge zur Kenntnis südasiatischer Sprachen und Literaturen 33. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. IV+138 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only professional descriptive grammar of Paniya (with texts and etymological dictionary) by a Nilgiri-languages specialist; §1 Phonetik und Phonologie pp. 7-9 has no accent heading in the TOC, but Kapp's other Nilgiri grammars carry short remarks on Akzent inside the phonology section, so this is the likeliest place for an explicit stress statement or an explicit silence of record. Nilgiris (Gudalur) variety.
sources.venue: Beiträge zur Kenntnis südasiatischer Sprachen und Literaturen
